That file is a webpack bundle: e.r(t), e.d(t,{Chatbot:()=>B, ..., default:()=>H}) defines a Chatbot getter returning the component B and a default getter returning H=B. The bundle ends with `H=B;module.exports=t`. So module.exports.Chatbot is the component, and the default is the same component. B is a plain function component (`const B=function(e){...}`). A grep for `B.<prop>=` static assignments found none, so the component has no static Chatbot member. src/widget/kitInterop.ts:7-8 returns `kitDefault.Chatbot ?? kitDefault`. With the whole exports object this gives B. With the component itself, Chatbot is undefined and the result is B. I did not read src/vendor.d.ts, because the grep for 'chatbot-kit' in view-head/src showed no hit in it. That does not change the runtime result. The minified-bundle check for statics is a grep, not an execution, but the module has a single exports assignment.

Node's cjs-module-lexer only detects literal exports.X= / Object.defineProperty(exports,...) / object-literal module.exports / require reexports, not `module.exports=<identifier>`, so `import { Chatbot }` under Node ESM cannot see Chatbot; the default import is the whole module.exports, with Chatbot as a property, matching the unwrap in src/widget/kitInterop.ts:7-9. Falsifying input considered: an ESM entry or lexer-recognised assignment; neither exists.
